query: Why do some Amazon products receive predominantly negative reviews, and which factors contribute the most?

per_column.name: content_word_count
per_column.rationale: Raw word count is a generic surface feature that offers weak analytical leverage for explaining WHY reviews are negative; review length correlates only loosely with sentiment drivers. Values are trivially and correctly derivable from the content text.

per_column.name: has_complaint_language
per_column.rationale: A complaint-language flag gives a genuine axis to group and compare negative reviews and identify contributing factors, directly serving the query. Values are mostly sound readings, though AMZ-0004 ('I do have one negative comment') arguably contains complaint language yet is flagged 0, indicating some noise.

per_column.name: has_praise_language
per_column.rationale: A praise flag complements the complaint flag and helps distinguish purely negative from mixed reviews, useful for isolating drivers of negativity. Groundedness is generally sound but AMZ-0004 ('can't get enough of it', 'keeps my skin clear') clearly contains praise yet is flagged 0, showing extraction errors.

per_column.name: has_negation_language
per_column.rationale: A bare negation-presence flag is largely skewed (171/250) and generic; negation appears in positive and negative reviews alike, so it adds limited leverage for explaining negativity. Values appear correctly derived from surface cues (n't, not, don't).

judge.rationale: The complaint/praise language flags provide real analytical axes to group and compare reviews and probe factors behind negative sentiment, satisfying the usefulness condition; the word-count and bare negation flags are more generic and weakly linked to the query. Values are broadly grounded in the source text and derivable from it, but the praise/complaint flags show observable misclassifications (notably AMZ-0004), tempering groundedness. No invented facts are asserted.
